items.title: Qantas cuts domestic flights and raises fares as fuel costs blow out
items.description: Qantas will cut domestic flights due to higher fuel costs and the uncertainty of the Middle East war, as it flags as much as $800 million in extra fuel costs.

items.title: Live: Several ships seen passing through the Strait of Hormuz as US blockade continues
items.description: US Vice-President JD Vance accuses the Iranian government of engaging in "economic terrorism" by blocking traffic through the Strait of Hormuz as the US Navy begins its blockade of Iran's ports. Follow live.

items.title: Fuel excise cut 'too focused on politics', analysts say as concerns grow
items.description: Some energy analysts are questioning the federal government's temporary tax cuts on fuel, warning that lower prices may work against Australia's long-term needs and goals.

items.title: The warning signs a health practitioner wants to exploit your superannuation
items.description: The healthcare regulator and tax office are cracking down on health practitioners who help patients access their superannuation early after one Perth doctor signed off on a $20,000 withdrawal for liposuction.

items.title: Live: Umpire '100 per cent adamant' he heard Butters sledge correctly
items.description: Port Adelaide's acting captain Zak Butters will face the AFL Tribunal to fight allegations he asked umpire Nick Foot "how much are they paying you?" during the game against St Kilda. Follow live.

items.title: Prince Harry and Meghan kick off Australia visit with stop at Melbourne hospital
items.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have begun their multi-day visit to Australia in Melbourne, meeting with patients at a children's hospital.

items.title: Palestinian groups take Australia to court over Israel arms exports
items.description: A group of Palestinian human rights organisations launch legal action against the defence minister seeking transparency over Australia's arms exports to Israel.

items.title: Live: Business confidence crashes to lowest level since April 2020
items.description: The outbreak of the war in the Middle East saw business confidence post its second-largest monthly fall on record, a NAB survey found. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Stagflation is a 'central banker's nightmare', says RBA deputy governor
items.description: RBA deputy governor Andrew Hauser says stagflation is a "central banker's nightmare" and the coming months will be challenging for Australia.

items.title: Harvey Weinstein to face retrial on New York rape charge
items.description: Former Hollywood magnate Harvey Weinstein is again going on trial on a rape charge in New York City. He will remain imprisoned for other offences regardless of the verdict.

items.title: 'Make a noise': The ordinary people who took their case to our highest court
items.description: From love and freedom to native title and the right to vote, these are some of the High Court cases that have helped define our nation, and the ordinary people behind them.

items.title: Safety alert issued amid explosion of illegal peptide use
items.description: The medicines regulator issues a health alert about the risks of using unregulated peptides amid a surge in the use of potentially unsafe injectables.

items.title: Matt Wright's former pilot faces court on crocodile egg stealing charge
items.description: Four men who were allegedly involved in a "sophisticated" operation to steal "hundreds" of crocodile eggs from Kakadu National Park have faced court in Darwin.

items.title: INXS is out, Phil Collins in as Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 2026 inductees announced
items.description: INXS has missed out on landing a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame with 2026 inductees including Phil Collins, Queen Latifah and Fela Kuti.

items.title: Kitty Flanagan and Anne Edmonds create comedy chaos in new show
items.description: Plus Nicole Kidman is an Aussie wrestler in Margo's Got Money Troubles, Baby Reindeer's Richard Gadd returns, and the reboots keep on coming with Malcolm in the Middle.

items.title: How I've learnt to embrace the new normal of only having one breast
items.description: I decided to keep my healthy breast, opting against reconstruction. It means I'm now what's known in the community as a uniboober.

items.title: Trump's 'AI Jesus' post sparks backlash as pope responds to attack
items.description: Donald Trump is criticised by religious sections of his supporter base after publishing, then deleting, the image, but the US president says: "I thought it was me as a doctor."

items.title: Australia's largest cattle feedlot on the market as grain-fed beef surges
items.description: Mort & Co, which fattens hundreds of thousands of cattle on grain before being slaughtered for beef, puts the majority of its assets on the market.

items.title: WA government says it has secured 4 million litres of diesel
items.description: Four million litres of diesel is set to arrive in Western Australia "in the coming weeks" as part of a strategic stockpile to address acute, localised fuel shortages across the state.

items.title: Financial, environmental and safety issues emerge at remote NT mine
items.description: Nathan River Resources has stood down more than 40 workers since Good Friday. Now financial, environmental and safety issues at the mine are being raised, as the NT government is accused of weak regulation.

items.title: Man says he was acting in 'self-defence' when he kicked a dog twice in the head
items.description: A northern suburbs man says he had been bitten and was acting in self-defence when he kicked a dog that was tethered to the tray of a ute in a Bunnings car park.

items.title: Colombia approves cull of up to 80 hippos
items.description: Colombian officials have authorised a plan to cull dozens of hippos, years after notorious drug lord Pablo Escobar brought in the first ones.

items.title: Incoming minister defends Setka friendship amid Victorian cabinet reshuffle
items.description: Four Labor MPs have been promoted to the Victorian government's ministry, with one of the incoming ministers defending her past support of disgraced CFMEU head John Setka.

items.title: Vanessa Bleyer to replace Peter Whish-Wilson in Senate
items.description: Tasmanian lawyer Vanessa Bleyer has been elected to replace outgoing Australian Greens senator for Tasmania, Peter Whish-Wilson.

items.title: WA government eyes off unused COVID quarantine facility for prison
items.description: The WA government flags the possible conversion of the Bullsbrook COVID quarantine centre into a prison amid an "unprecedented" rise in the number of inmates being crammed into cells across the state.
